3.notes:
1.  mkdir -p ~/lab/week1: This creates a new folder (directory) called “week1” inside your “lab” folder. The -p option tells it to create parent folders if they don’t already exist.
2.  cd ~/lab/week1: This command changes your current location in the terminal to the “week1” folder.
3.  touch test1.txt test2.txt: This creates two empty files named “test1.txt” and “test2.txt” within the “week1” folder. touch is used to create new, empty files or update the timestamp of existing files.
4.  cp test1.txt test1_copy.txt: This copies the file “test1.txt” and creates a new file named “test1_copy.txt” with the same contents.
5.  mv test1_copy.txt test1.txt: This moves (and effectively renames) the file “test1_copy.txt” back to “test1.txt”.
6.  ls -la: This lists all files and folders in the current directory (the “week1” folder), including hidden files (files that start with a “.”). The -l option gives you a detailed listing, and the -a option includes hidden files.
